commit_scope: Restore the Hati grocery balance from its connected Sheet, resolve production-shaped legacy presence identities, and keep large substrate recipes deployable on PostgreSQL.
evidence_refs: The merged deployment installed SHA 61070d093bcc5614ad95e3029b58d190bd500f4b, but /people/urs-muff/edit still rendered the soft-404 page.
The source-backed Urs graph record declares legacy_ids containing urs-muff; the first resolver implementation queried aliases only.
The failed Hostinger rollout log showed PostgreSQL rejecting a 10877-character recipe value because uq_substrate_serialized exceeded the btree index-row limit.

The Google Sheets connector verified the configured Hati Suci - Food workbook, its Sheet1 summary formulas, and a current calculated balance without reading or recording household transaction rows in this receipt.
The app contract was write-only: it mirrored graph entries into Sheets but calculated remaining balance solely from graph rows, excluding the pre-app ledger history.
The first repair read the anonymous CSV export and trusted sheet_synced as an atomic boundary; exact-head review exposed both the privacy leak and the append/flag crash race before merge.

The repaired carrier authenticates every request, returns only Sisa plus matches among caller-supplied pending entry IDs, and makes appends idempotent with an Entry ID column; the spreadsheet can remain private.

New graph writes carry the entry-id-v1 protocol marker; unmarked unsynced legacy rows remain explicitly unknown, make balance unavailable, and are excluded from automatic replay or deletion until migrated.

Historical-baseline availability and the signed pending fold now execute in endpoint_grocery_remaining.fk; an unavailable Sheet produces an explicit unavailable balance rather than an incomplete graph-only number.

Deletion uses one Apps Script lock to serialize original appends, a private durable cancellation marker, and the stable reversal; it preserves the graph row on uncertainty and physically removes it only after the atomic carrier receipt.

Every generic graph query surface rejects or omits grocery_spend nodes and their connected edges, including list, detail, revisions, edges, neighbors, subgraph, path, counts, stats, proof, profiles, and resonance; generic PATCH and DELETE also reject them.

The Apps Script summary returns both acknowledged and cancelled subsets under the same lock; a deletion completed after the database snapshot therefore cannot leave a stale pending amount in the returned balance.

The developer quick-start timing witness explicitly loads the required pytest-asyncio plugin while disabling unrelated host plugin autoload, keeping the ten-second gate deterministic under a busy local Form body.
The documented Sheet restructure preserves existing Entry IDs across re-runs instead of erasing the idempotency ledger.
The restructure now holds the same Apps Script lock for its full snapshot-and-rewrite interval, excluding concurrent append and delete operations.

Grocery reconciliation reads every row with one immutable-ID-ordered database statement before declaring the legacy-unknown set empty; a 2,001-row focused witness proves there is no page ceiling or mutable OFFSET seam.
Graph identity lookup now recognizes both aliases and legacy_ids with indexed JSON containment and exact membership confirmation.
PostgreSQL substrate uniqueness now uses a bounded md5 expression key while exact full serialized text remains part of every lookup; SQLite retains exact tuple uniqueness.
A PostgreSQL uniqueness-migration failure now clears the cached engine and raises through startup, guaranteeing the supervisor retries the complete schema gate instead of serving the old constraint.
PostgreSQL startup reads durable catalog state and skips both locking DDL statements once the legacy constraint is absent and the digest index exists.
The outer lifespan database-table gate now propagates schema failures instead of logging and continuing startup.
No private profile content is included in this receipt.
